proposals.before: When Wenheti's son Heduo Han and other splinter chiefs dragged their clans westward, deserting their father, Fei overtook them at Shangjun with a flying column and took Heduo Han's head.
proposals.after: When the Rouran splinter lord Wenheti's son Heduo Han and others led their clans westward, deserting their father, Fei overtook them at Shangjun with a flying column and took Heduo Han's head.
proposals.reason: Chinese 蠕蠕別主 modifies 縕紇提 (Wenheti), not Heduo Han; the idiomatic English makes Heduo Han himself a splinter chief.

proposals.before: Helin came after him with four thousand foot and horse as far as the Bosi River; Fei wheeled from Weichang, struck, and seized two hundred armored riders.
proposals.after: Helin came after him with four thousand foot and horse as far as the Gu River; Fei wheeled from Weichang, struck, and seized two hundred armored riders.
proposals.reason: 泒水 is the Gu River (Gushui), not the Bosi River; 波斯 would be Bosi.

proposals.before: Helin with four thousand foot and horse pursued Fei to the Bosi River; Fei from Weichang struck them and took two hundred armored riders.
proposals.after: Helin with four thousand foot and horse pursued Fei to the Gu River; Fei from Weichang struck them and took two hundred armored riders.
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise renders 泒水 as Bosi River, a different toponym.

proposals.before: Zhun took the bait and followed; he called himself Bearer of the Staff, Grand General Who Pacifies the West, Governor of Qing and Ji, Duke of Julu, with Ru as chief clerk. More than two thousand men rallied at Guancheng, the Dingling were drawn in, magistrates were cut down, and rebellion spread through Changshan, Julu, and Guangping.
proposals.after: Zhun took the bait and followed; he called himself Bearer of the Staff, Grand General Who Campaigns West, Governor of Qing and Ji, Duke of Julu, with Ru as chief clerk. More than two thousand men rallied at Guancheng, the Dingling were drawn in, magistrates were cut down, and rebellion spread through Changshan, Julu, and Guangping.
proposals.reason: 征西大將軍 is the general who campaigns westward, not who pacifies the west (安西).

proposals.before: Zhun rejoiced and followed him; he styled himself Bearer of the Staff, Grand General Who Pacifies the West, Governor of Qing and Ji provinces, Duke of Julu—Ru as chief clerk; they gathered a party of more than two thousand, held Guancheng, linked with the Dingling, killed chief officials, and stirred Changshan, Julu, and Guangping commanderies.
proposals.after: Zhun rejoiced and followed him; he styled himself Bearer of the Staff, Grand General Who Campaigns West, Governor of Qing and Ji provinces, Duke of Julu—Ru as chief clerk; they gathered a party of more than two thousand, held Guancheng, linked with the Dingling, killed chief officials, and stirred Changshan, Julu, and Guangping commanderies.
proposals.reason: Literal English repeats the 征西/pacifies mistranslation.

proposals.before: Under Shizu he marched on Pingliang; merit made him Marquis of Changjin and governor of Hejian.
proposals.after: Under Shizu he marched on Pingliang; merit made him Viscount of Changjin and governor of Hejian.
proposals.reason: Chinese 長進子 is a viscount (zi), not a marquis (hou); the idiomatic rendering upgrades the rank.

proposals.before: In Shizu's time he followed the campaign against Pingliang; for merit he was enfeoffed Marquis of Changjin and appointed governor of Hejian.
proposals.after: In Shizu's time he followed the campaign against Pingliang; for merit he was enfeoffed Viscount of Changjin and appointed governor of Hejian.
proposals.reason: Chinese 長進子 is a viscount (zi), not a marquis (hou); the literal rendering upgrades the rank.

proposals.before: Chen was the younger brother of Lan.
proposals.after: Chen's younger brother was Lan.
proposals.reason: Chinese 陳弟蘭 follows the chapter pattern X弟Y (Y is younger brother of X), matching 受興弟陳; the idiomatic English reversed the brothers.

proposals.before: Chen, younger brother of Lan.
proposals.after: Chen's younger brother Lan.
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise treats Chen as Lan's younger brother; the Chinese introduces Lan as Chen's younger brother.

proposals.before: Merit at the fall of Pingliang won him Marquis of Suiyang and the added rank Inspiring Martial Might General.
proposals.after: Merit at the fall of Pingliang won him viscount of Suiyang and the added rank Inspiring Martial Might General.
proposals.reason: 賜爵睢陽子 is a viscount (子), not a marquis (侯).

proposals.before: Later, for merit in breaking Pingliang, he was enfeoffed Marquis of Suiyang and given the additional title Inspiring Martial Might General.
proposals.after: Later, for merit in breaking Pingliang, he was enfeoffed viscount of Suiyang and given the additional title Inspiring Martial Might General.
proposals.reason: The rank 子 is viscount, not marquis.

proposals.before: On the Pingliang campaign merit won him Marquis of Lincheng, supernumerary attendant-in-ordinary, and Broad Martial General.
proposals.after: On the Pingliang campaign merit won him viscount of Lincheng, supernumerary attendant-in-ordinary, and Broad Martial General.
proposals.reason: 賜爵臨城子 is viscount (子), not marquis.

proposals.before: He followed the campaign against Pingliang; for merit he was enfeoffed Marquis of Lincheng and appointed supernumerary attendant-in-ordinary and Broad Martial General.
proposals.after: He followed the campaign against Pingliang; for merit he was enfeoffed viscount of Lincheng and appointed supernumerary attendant-in-ordinary and Broad Martial General.
proposals.reason: 臨城子 is viscount, not marquis.

proposals.before: Wu'er's younger brother Tu was chief clerk of Shuozhou, the record states.
proposals.after: Wu'er's younger brother Tu was chief clerk of Shuozhou.
proposals.reason: The Chinese has no phrase corresponding to 'the record states'; that clause is an invention.

proposals.before: He died; his son Yiwani succeeded.
proposals.after: He died; his son Yiwan succeeded.
proposals.reason: 億萬 is Yiwan; the extra final i in Yiwani is not supported by the Chinese.

proposals.before: At the siege of Zhongshan Nuo was first over the wall and lost an eye.
proposals.after: At the siege of Zhongshan, Nuo was first over the wall and lost an eye.
proposals.reason: Missing comma fuses the place Zhongshan with the person Nuo.

proposals.before: He was moved to general who pacifies the east and advanced to Duke of Wuling.
proposals.after: He was moved to General Who Calms the East and advanced to Duke of Wuling.
proposals.reason: 寧東將軍 is distinct from earlier 平東將軍; pacifies collapses that contrast.

proposals.before: Under Shizu more than two hundred men of Ji, Zhang Guangda among them, came to court to ask for him back; he was again named general who establishes the east and inspector of Youzhou, with his fief changed to Duke of Liaoxi.
proposals.after: Under Shizu more than two hundred men of Ji, Zhang Guangda among them, came to court to ask for him back; he was again named General Who Pacifies the East and inspector of Youzhou, with his fief changed to Duke of Liaoxi.
proposals.reason: 安東將軍 is pacify/secure the east; establishes renders 建, not 安.

proposals.before: He died in the Yanhe era, the record states.
proposals.after: He died in the Yanhe era.
proposals.reason: Chinese is only 延和中卒; the record states is invented.

proposals.before: His eighth son Guan[3] inherited the title, the record states.
proposals.after: His eighth son Guan inherited the title.
proposals.reason: Chinese has no the record states; keep the note marker only if a note exists, but the added narrator tag is not in the source.

proposals.before: When Shizu took the throne, he ordered Juan, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry Liu Kuren, and eight others to divide charge of the four departments and manage key memorials.
proposals.after: When Shizu took the throne, he ordered Juan, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry Liu Kuren, and the rest, eight men in all, to divide charge of the four departments and manage key memorials.
proposals.reason: 等八人 means a group of eight including the named men, not eight additional men.

proposals.before: The Rouran chief Mogao came against him with five thousand Gaoche riders; Juan broke them and took more than a thousand heads.
proposals.after: The Rouran chief Mogu came against him with five thousand Gaoche riders; Juan broke them and took more than a thousand heads.
proposals.reason: Chinese 莫孤 is Mogu, not Mogao.

proposals.before: Juan and the attending censor An Pi laid an ambush in secret, intercepted Chang, and took him alive.
proposals.after: Juan and the attending censor An Jie laid an ambush in secret, intercepted Chang, and took him alive.
proposals.reason: 安頡 is An Jie; An Pi does not match the given name 頡.

proposals.before: Juan with Attending Censor An Pi secretly set an ambush, intercepted and captured Chang.
proposals.after: Juan with Attending Censor An Jie secretly set an ambush, intercepted and captured Chang.
proposals.reason: 安頡 is An Jie; An Pi does not match the given name 頡.

proposals.before: Merit made him general who pacifies the north and palace attendant, and his title rose to Duke of Yuyang.
proposals.after: Merit made him General Who Tranquilizes the North and palace attendant, and his title rose to Duke of Yuyang.
proposals.reason: 寧北將軍 is distinct from the earlier 安北將軍 and should not be flattened to the same English office.

proposals.before: His son Duohou succeeded him the title.
proposals.after: His son Duohou succeeded to the title.
proposals.reason: English is ungrammatical; 襲爵 means he inherited the title.

proposals.before: His son Jian succeeded him the title.
proposals.after: His son Jian succeeded to the title.
proposals.reason: English is ungrammatical; 襲爵 means he inherited the title.

proposals.before: He served as attendant.
proposals.after: He served as Attendant of the Inner Court.
proposals.reason: 給事中 is a specific inner-court office, not a generic attendant.

proposals.before: He died without sons, the record states.
proposals.after: He died without sons.
proposals.reason: The Chinese has only 卒，無子; the phrase the record states is an invented narrator tag.

proposals.before: Jian's younger brother Na inherited the title, the record states.
proposals.after: Jian's younger brother Na inherited the title.
proposals.reason: The Chinese has only 建弟那，襲爵; the phrase the record states is an invented narrator tag.

proposals.before: Under Gaozu he doffed the hemp and became outside-the-gates attendant-in-ordinary on the casual staff, then rose by degrees to left general and grand master of splendid happiness.
proposals.after: Under Gaozu he doffed the hemp and became supernumerary cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, then rose by degrees to left general and grand master of splendid happiness.
proposals.reason: 員外散騎侍郎 is a supernumerary cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, not an outside-the-gates post.

proposals.before: In Gaozu's time he doffed the hemp and was made Outside-the-Gates Attendant-in-Ordinary on the Casual Staff, then gradually rose to Left General and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
proposals.after: In Gaozu's time he doffed the hemp and was made Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, then gradually rose to Left General and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
proposals.reason: 員外 marks an extra-establishment post, not outside-the-gates.

proposals.before: Qingbin's aide Yao He opened the gates from within; Rong killed Qingbin's staff, seized Qingbin, and carried him to Xiurong, calling him "foster father."
proposals.after: Qingbin's attendant officer Yao He opened the gates from within; Rong killed Qingbin's staff, seized Qingbin, and carried him to Xiurong, calling him "foster father."
proposals.reason: 別駕 is the provincial attendant officer, not a generic aide.

proposals.before: Qingbin's aide Yao He colluded within; Rong then killed Qingbin's staff, seized Qingbin and brought him back to Xiurong, calling him "foster father."
proposals.after: Qingbin's attendant officer Yao He colluded within; Rong then killed Qingbin's staff, seized Qingbin and brought him back to Xiurong, calling him "foster father."
proposals.reason: 別駕 should not be flattened to aide.

proposals.before: Under Emperor Ming he acted for Ying Province and fell fighting Liang general Pei Zhili.
proposals.after: Under Suzong he acted for Ying Province and fell fighting Liang general Pei Zhili.
proposals.reason: The Chinese names 肅宗, already rendered Suzong in this chapter; Emperor Ming invites confusion with Taizong Mingyuan.

proposals.before: His younger brother Zhuangde inherited the title, the record states.
proposals.after: His younger brother Zhuangde inherited the title.
proposals.reason: The Chinese has no equivalent of 'the record states'.

proposals.before: Guzhen's sixth-generation collateral descendant Yu, styled Chenxing, was stiffly upright.
proposals.after: Guzhen's collateral xuansun Yu, styled Chenxing, was stiffly upright.
proposals.reason: 玄孫 is a great-great-grandson, not a sixth-generation descendant; 族 marks a collateral line.

proposals.before: Guzhen's collateral descendant by the sixth generation, Yu, style name Chenxing, was upright by nature.
proposals.after: Guzhen's collateral xuansun Yu, style name Chenxing, was upright by nature.
proposals.reason: Same 玄孫 generation error as the idiomatic line.

proposals.before: Under Emperor Ming he was general of the martial guard.
proposals.after: Under Suzong he was general of the martial guard.
proposals.reason: Chinese is 肅宗, rendered Suzong elsewhere in the chapter.

proposals.before: The Wei brothers were loyal and fierce, roused to the utmost pitch, and for duty's sake forgot their lives.
proposals.after: The Wei Guzhen brothers were loyal and fierce, roused to the utmost pitch, and for duty's sake forgot their lives.
proposals.reason: 尉真 names Guzhen; dropping it leaves only a surname collective.

proposals.before: The same below; not listed again, the record states.
proposals.after: The same below; not listed again.
proposals.reason: Chinese 下同，不再列舉 has no narrator phrase matching 'the record states'; that clause is an invention.

proposals.before: "The eighth son Guan": Northern History juan 20, Wei Guzhen's life, has "Guan" as "Huan."
proposals.after: "The eighth son Guan": Northern History juan 20, biography of Wei Guzhen, has "Guan" as "Huan."
proposals.reason: 傳 is the biography, not an unspecified 'life'; the idiomatic English should name the biography of Wei Guzhen.
